claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows from the definition in claim 1 (the principle constrains how new cases arrive; .NET docs frame it as adding subscribers "without the need to modify the sender service"). Lesson wording is scoped to the example (moving the standard threshold edits StandardShipping), not stated as a universal rule.

Direct consequence of claim 1 applied to a type-checking caller: a caller that lists kinds by class must be edited for each new kind, which is modification. Lesson states it with a condition ("If callers checked which class they had").

git grep -n -E "StandardShipping|ExpressShipping|PickUpInStore|new .*Shipping" stage-1 over the whole repo: the only `new` of these classes are SamplesTests.cs:12 `ShippingFee fee = new StandardShipping();` and SamplesTests.cs:21 `new ShippingFee[] { new StandardShipping(), new ExpressShipping(), new PickUpInStore() }`. No production code creates them. Note: two tests, not one (see issue on section 4).

issues.text: At stage-1 two tests in SamplesTests.cs create the kinds: StandardShippingIsFreeFromTwoMillion (line 12, `new StandardShipping()`) and EveryKindAnswersTheSameCall (line 21, all three). "the only place ... is a test" is off by one; the file-level statement (claim 10) is correct.
issues.quote: the only place that creates the kinds is a test in `SamplesTests.cs`, which writes `new StandardShipping()` and the others
issues.fix: Replace with: "the only code that creates the kinds is two tests in `SamplesTests.cs`, which write `new StandardShipping()` and the others".

issues.text: Explanation b reasons backwards and ignores the source: `ExpressShipping` is `sealed` at stage-1, so option b cannot compile; and the base class matters only because the caller checks classes by name (deriving from ExpressShipping would make `is ExpressShipping` match). Key (a) remains correct.

issues.text: Core concepts says adding a case should not require editing working code. Here the lesson admits an edit is still needed 'where the kind is chosen', then says it is fine because it is 'outside the fee rules'. I cannot picture where that place is (no code shows it) or why editing it does not break OCP by the lesson's own definition. I stopped here.
issues.quote: Some code still has to create the new kind, and that may mean a small edit where the kind is chosen; but it sits outside the fee rules, and the rules that already work are not edited.
issues.fix: Add one sentence naming a concrete spot, e.g. 'the line that writes `new StandardShipping()` when an order picks standard', and one sentence saying OCP protects the fee rules and their tests; that one creation line is the only place that learns the new name.

issues.quote: the next SOLID principle: every new subtype must keep the promise its base type makes.
issues.fix: Replace 'every new subtype' with 'every new class that derives from a base type'.
